correctness.rationale: The direct rational-gradient equations give a bijection with nonzero t satisfying b=t^5-t^3. The q-3 incidence count excludes only t=±1. Frobenius-term Taylor expansion gives the precise Hessian determinant 2t(2t²-3). The lower two-by-two minor rules out corank greater than one. At Hessian-degenerate points, a kernel direction gives order at least three on a rational line and the other q rational points yield q+3 intersection multiplicity against degree q+2, forcing containment. Full derivatives and projective points were checked independently over p=3,5,7,11,13,19. No extrapolation from finite computation is used.

value.rationale: The q+2 companion construction is a recently motivated minimal-degree space-filling family. Describing its exact rational singularity incidence and ordinary-node boundary supplies intrinsic geometry of its degenerations and a forcing phenomenon (contained Fq-lines) at a sharp square-class boundary. Unlike an arbitrary finite table, the theorem holds for every odd prime power and makes a structural prediction relevant to separating smooth from rationally smooth choices.
